sanskrit: bāṇajālaṃ diviṣṭhaṃ tat svarṇajālavibhūṣitam śuśubhe bharataśreṣṭha vitānam iva viṣṭhitam
english: That web of arrows poised in the sky, adorned with a meshwork of gold, shone forth, O best of the Bharatas, like a great canopy stretched overhead.

sanskrit: tena channe raṇe rājan bāṇajālena bhāsvatā abhracchāyeva saṃjajñe bāṇaruddhe nabhastale
english: With that gleaming net of arrows veiling the battle, O king, a shade as of clouds arose, the very sky barred over by shafts.

sanskrit: tatrāścaryam apaśyāma bāṇabhūte tathāvidhe na sma saṃpatate bhūmau dṛṣṭvā drauṇeḥ parākramam
english: There we beheld a marvel, where such a thicket of arrows had formed: beholding the prowess of Droṇa's son, not one shaft fell to the ground.

sanskrit: lāghavaṃ droṇaputrasya dṛṣṭvā tatra mahārathāḥ vyasmayanta mahārāja na cainaṃ prativīkṣitum śekus te sarvarājānas tapantam iva bhāskaram
english: Beholding the deftness of Droṇa's son, the great chariot-warriors were struck with wonder, O great king; and all those kings could not so much as look upon him, as upon the burning sun.

sanskrit: sātyakir yatamānas tu dharmarājaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ tathetarāṇi sainyāni na sma cakruḥ parākramam
english: Though Sātyaki strove, and the King of Righteousness, the son of Pāṇḍu, and the other hosts as well, they could mount no prowess against him.

sanskrit: vadhyamāne tataḥ sainye draupadeyā mahārathāḥ sātyakir dharmarājaś ca pāñcālāś cāpi saṃgatāḥ tyaktvā mṛtyubhayaṃ ghoraṃ drauṇāyanim upādravan
english: Then, as the host was being slaughtered, the great chariot-warriors who were Draupadī's sons, Sātyaki and the King of Righteousness, and the Pāñcālas too, all joined together; and casting off the dread fear of death, they rushed upon the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: sātyakiḥ pañcaviṃśatyā drauṇiṃ viddhvā śilāmukhaiḥ punar vivyādha nārācaiḥ saptabhiḥ svarṇabhūṣitaiḥ
english: Sātyaki, having pierced Droṇa's son with twenty-five stone-tipped shafts, pierced him again with seven gold-adorned iron arrows.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras trisaptatyā prativindhyaś ca saptabhiḥ śrutakarmā tribhir bāṇaiḥ śrutakīrtis tu saptabhiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira struck him with seventy-three, Prativindhya with seven, Śrutakarman with three arrows, and Śrutakīrti with seven.

sanskrit: sutasomaś ca navabhiḥ śatānīkaś ca saptabhiḥ anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā vivyadhus taṃ samantataḥ
english: Sutasoma with nine and Śatānīka with seven, and many other heroes pierced him on every side.

sanskrit: so 'tikruddhas tato rājann āśīviṣa iva śvasan sātyakiṃ pañcaviṃśatyā prāvidhyata śilāśitaiḥ
english: Then he, exceedingly wrathful, O king, hissing like a venomous serpent, pierced Sātyaki with twenty-five stone-whetted shafts.

sanskrit: śrutakīrtiṃ ca navabhiḥ sutasomaṃ ca pañcabhiḥ aṣṭabhiḥ śrutakarmāṇaṃ prativindhyaṃ tribhiḥ śaraiḥ śatānīkaṃ ca navabhir dharmaputraṃ ca saptabhiḥ
english: Śrutakīrti with nine and Sutasoma with five, Śrutakarman with eight and Prativindhya with three arrows, Śatānīka with nine and the son of Dharma with seven.

sanskrit: athetarāṃs tataḥ śūrān dvābhyāṃ dvābhyām atāḍayat śrutakīrtes tathā cāpaṃ ciccheda niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then he smote the other heroes with two shafts apiece, and with sharpened arrows he cut asunder the bow of Śrutakīrti.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya śrutakīrtir mahārathaḥ drauṇāyaniṃ tribhir viddhvā vivyādhānyaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, taking up another bow, Śrutakīrti the great chariot-warrior pierced Droṇa's son with three shafts and struck him again with other whetted arrows.

sanskrit: tato drauṇir mahārāja śaravarṣeṇa bhārata chādayām āsa tat sainyaṃ samantāc ca śarair nṛpān
english: Then Droṇa's son, O great king, O Bhārata, with a torrent of arrows enveloped that host, and the kings on every side with his shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar ameyātmā dharmarājasya kārmukam drauṇiś ciccheda vihasan vivyādha ca śarais tribhiḥ
english: Then again the immeasurable-souled son of Droṇa, laughing, cut asunder the bow of the King of Righteousness and pierced him with three arrows.

sanskrit: tato dharmasuto rājan pragṛhyānyan mahad dhanuḥ drauṇiṃ vivyādha saptatyā bāhvor urasi cārdayat
english: Then the son of Dharma, O king, taking up another mighty bow, pierced the son of Droṇa with seventy shafts and afflicted him in the arms and breast.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu tataḥ kruddho drauṇeḥ praharato raṇe ardhacandreṇa tīkṣṇena dhanuś chittvānadad bhṛśam
english: Then Sātyaki, enraged, with a sharp crescent-headed arrow cut the bow of Droṇa's son as he struck in the battle, and roared aloud.

sanskrit: chinnadhanvā tato drauṇiḥ śaktyā śaktimatāṃ varaḥ sārathiṃ pātayām āsa śaineyasya rathād drutam
english: His bow cut, Droṇa's son then, foremost of the mighty, with a spear swiftly struck down the charioteer of the Śaineya from his car.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya droṇaputraḥ pratāpavān śaineyaṃ śaravarṣeṇa chādayām āsa bhārata
english: Then, taking up another bow, the mighty son of Droṇa enveloped the Śaineya with a downpour of arrows, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tasyāśvāḥ pradrutāḥ saṃkhye patite rathasārathau tatra tatraiva dhāvantaḥ samadṛśyanta bhārata
english: His horses, the chariot-driver fallen in the fray, bolted in flight, and were seen running this way and that, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirapurogās te drauṇiṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ varam abhyavarṣanta vegena visṛjantaḥ śitāñ śarān
english: Then those warriors, with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head, rained upon the son of Droṇa, foremost of weapon-bearers, with force loosing their whetted shafts.

sanskrit: āgacchamānāṃs tān dṛṣṭvā raudrarūpān paraṃtapaḥ prahasan pratijagrāha droṇaputro mahāraṇe
english: Beholding them advancing in fearful aspect, the scorcher of foes, the son of Droṇa, laughing, received them in the great battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraśatajvālaḥ senākakṣaṃ mahārathaḥ drauṇir dadāha samare kakṣam agnir yathā vane
english: Then the great chariot-warrior, son of Droṇa, blazing with a hundred shafts for his flames, burned up the thicket of the army in battle as fire burns dry brush in the forest.

sanskrit: tad balaṃ pāṇḍuputrasya droṇaputrapratāpitam cukṣubhe bharataśreṣṭha timineva nadīmukham
english: That army of the son of Pāṇḍu, scorched by Droṇa's son, was thrown into tumult, O best of the Bharatas, as a river's mouth is troubled by a great sea-monster.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā te ca mahārāja droṇaputraparākramam nihatān menire sarvān pāṇḍūn droṇasutena vai
english: And beholding, O great king, the prowess of Droṇa's son, they deemed all the Pāṇḍavas already slain by the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu tvarito drauṇiṃ śliṣya mahāratham abravīd droṇaputraṃ tu roṣāmarṣasamanvitaḥ
english: But Yudhiṣṭhira in haste closed with the son of Droṇa, that great chariot-warrior, and spoke to him, filled with wrath and indignation:

sanskrit: naiva nāma tava prītir naiva nāma kṛtajñatā yatas tvaṃ puruṣavyāghra mām evādya jighāṃsasi
english: "You have, it seems, no affection, nor any gratitude, O tiger among men, that you seek this very day to slay me."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇena tapaḥ kāryaṃ dānam adhyayanaṃ tathā kṣatriyeṇa dhanur nāmyaṃ sa bhavān brāhmaṇabruvaḥ
english: "By a brāhmaṇa austerity must be practiced, and giving, and study; by a kṣatriya the bow must be bent. You are a brāhmaṇa only in name."

sanskrit: miṣatas te mahābāho jeṣyāmi yudhi kauravān kuruṣva samare karma brahmabandhur asi dhruvam
english: "Before your very eyes, O mighty-armed one, I shall vanquish the Kauravas in battle. Do your deed in the fray; you are surely but a brāhmaṇa in name only."

sanskrit: evam ukto mahārāja droṇaputraḥ smayann iva yuktatvaṃ tac ca saṃcintya nottaraṃ kiṃ cid abravīt
english: Thus addressed, O great king, the son of Droṇa, smiling as it were, and reflecting on the justice of it, made no reply at all.

sanskrit: anuktvā ca tataḥ kiṃ cic charavarṣeṇa pāṇḍavam chādayām āsa samare kruddho 'ntaka iva prajāḥ
english: And saying nothing further, he covered the son of Pāṇḍu in battle with a torrent of arrows, wrathful as Death covering all creatures.

sanskrit: saṃchādyamānas tu tadā droṇaputreṇa māriṣa pārtho 'payātaḥ śīghraṃ vai vihāya mahatīṃ camūm
english: Being thus covered then by the son of Droṇa, O honored one, the Pārtha swiftly withdrew, abandoning his great host.

sanskrit: apayāte tatas tasmin dharmaputre yudhiṣṭhire droṇaputraḥ sthito rājan pratyādeśān mahātmanaḥ
english: When that son of Dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira, had withdrawn, the son of Droṇa stood firm, O king, beyond reproach of the great-souled one.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā tyaktvā drauṇiṃ mahāhave prayayau tāvakaṃ sainyaṃ yuktaḥ krūrāya karmaṇe
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, leaving the son of Droṇa in that great battle, set forth against your host, intent upon a cruel deed.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhīmasenaṃ sapāñcālyaṃ cedikekayasaṃvṛtam vaikartanaḥ svayaṃ ruddhvā vārayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Vaikartana himself, holding back Bhīmasena—accompanied by the Pāñcāla, hemmed about by the Cedis and the Kekayas—checked him with his shafts.

sanskrit: tatas tu cedikārūṣān sṛñjayāṃś ca mahārathān karṇo jaghāna saṃkruddho bhīmasenasya paśyataḥ
english: Then Karṇa, exceedingly enraged, slew the Cedis, the Kārūṣas, and the Sṛñjaya great chariot-warriors before the very eyes of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tataḥ karṇaṃ vihāya rathasattamam prayayau kauravaṃ sainyaṃ kakṣam agnir iva jvalan
english: Then Bhīmasena, leaving Karṇa, that best of chariot-warriors, advanced upon the Kaurava host, blazing like fire upon dry brushwood.

sanskrit: sūtaputro 'pi samare pāñcālān kekayāṃs tathā sṛñjayāṃś ca maheṣvāsān nijaghāna sahasraśaḥ
english: The son of the sūta too, in battle, slew the Pāñcālas and the Kekayas, and the great-bowmen Sṛñjayas, by the thousands.

sanskrit: saṃśaptakeṣu pārthaś ca kauraveṣu vṛkodaraḥ pāñcāleṣu tathā karṇaḥ kṣayaṃ cakrūr mahārathāḥ
english: Among the saṃśaptakas the Pārtha, among the Kauravas Vṛkodara, and among the Pāñcālas Karṇa—those great chariot-warriors wrought havoc.

sanskrit: te kṣatriyā dahyamānās tribhis taiḥ pāvakopamaiḥ jagmur vināśaṃ samare rājan durmantrite tava
english: Those warriors, consumed by those three who were like fire, went to destruction in the battle, O king, through your evil counsel.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ kruddho nakulaṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha bharataśreṣṭha caturaś cāsya vājinaḥ
english: Then Duryodhana, enraged, pierced Nakula with nine arrows, O best of the Bharatas, and his four steeds as well.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar ameyātmā tava putro janādhipaḥ kṣureṇa sahadevasya dhvajaṃ ciccheda kāñcanam
english: Then again your son, the immeasurable-souled lord of men, with a razor-headed shaft cut down the golden standard of Sahadeva.

sanskrit: nakulas tu tataḥ kruddhas tava putraṃ trisaptabhiḥ jaghāna samare rājan sahadevaś ca pañcabhiḥ
english: Then Nakula, enraged, struck your son with twenty-one shafts in the battle, O king, and Sahadeva with five.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau bharataśreṣṭhau śreṣṭhau sarvadhanuṣmatām vivyādhorasi saṃkruddhaḥ pañcabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Both those best of the Bharatas, foremost of all bowmen, he in great wrath pierced in the breast, with five arrows and five.

sanskrit: tato 'parābhyāṃ bhallābhyāṃ dhanuṣī samakṛntata yamayoḥ prahasan rājan vivyādhaiva ca saptabhiḥ
english: Then with two more broad-headed arrows he cut through the bows of the twins, O king, laughing, and pierced them with seven.

sanskrit: tāv anye dhanuṣī śreṣṭhe śakracāpanibhe śubhe pragṛhya rejatuḥ śūrau devaputrasamau yudhi
english: Taking up two other bows, fair and excellent, resembling the bow of Indra, those two heroes shone in the fray, like the sons of the gods.

sanskrit: tatas tau rabhasau yuddhe bhrātarau bhrātaraṃ nṛpa śarair vavarṣatur ghorair mahāmeghau yathācalam
english: Then those two impetuous brothers, O king, rained dreadful arrows upon their brother in the battle, as two great clouds upon a mountain.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja tava putro mahārathaḥ pāṇḍuputrau maheṣvāsau vārayām āsa patribhiḥ
english: Then, enraged, O great king, your son, the great chariot-warrior, held back the two great-bowmen sons of Pāṇḍu with his feathered shafts.

sanskrit: dhanurmaṇḍalam evāsya dṛśyate yudhi bhārata sāyakāś caiva dṛśyante niścarantaḥ samantataḥ
english: His bow alone was seen as a circle in the battle, O Bhārata, and the arrows were seen issuing forth on every side.

sanskrit: tasya sāyakasaṃchannau cakāśetāṃ ca pāṇḍavau meghacchannau yathā vyomni candrasūryau hataprabhau
english: Veiled by his shafts, the two sons of Pāṇḍu gleamed forth like the moon and the sun in the sky, cloud-shrouded, their radiance dimmed.

sanskrit: te tu bāṇā mahārāja hemapuṅkhāḥ śilāśitāḥ ācchādayan diśaḥ sarvāḥ sūryasyevāṃśavas tadā
english: And those arrows, O great king, gold-feathered and stone-whetted, covered all the quarters then, like the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: bāṇabhūte tatas tasmin saṃchanne ca nabhastale yamābhyāṃ dadṛśe rūpaṃ kālāntakayamopamam
english: When the sky had thus become a thicket of arrows and was veiled over, the form of the twins appeared like Yama, the all-ending Death.

sanskrit: parākramaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā tava sūnor mahārathāḥ mṛtyor upāntikaṃ prāptau mādrīputrau sma menire
english: Beholding that prowess of your son, the great chariot-warriors deemed the two sons of Mādrī to have come near to death.

sanskrit: tataḥ senāpatī rājan pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ pārṣataḥ prayayau tatra yatra rājā suyodhanaḥ
english: Then the commander of the host of the great-souled Pāṇḍava, the son of Pṛṣata, O king, advanced thither, where King Suyodhana was.

sanskrit: mādrīputrau tataḥ śūrau vyatikramya mahārathau dhṛṣṭadyumnas tava sutaṃ tāḍayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: Then, passing beyond the two heroic great chariot-warriors who were Mādrī's sons, Dhṛṣṭadyumna smote your son with his shafts.

sanskrit: tam avidhyad ameyātmā tava putro 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ pāñcālyaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā prahasya puruṣarṣabha
english: Him the immeasurable-souled, exceedingly impatient son of yours pierced—the Pāñcāla prince—with twenty-five shafts, laughing, O bull among men.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar ameyātmā putras te pṛthivīpate viddhvā nanāda pāñcālyaṃ ṣaṣṭyā pañcabhir eva ca
english: Then again the immeasurable-souled son of yours, O lord of the earth, having pierced the Pāñcāla prince with sixty-five, roared aloud.

sanskrit: athāsya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ hastāvāpaṃ ca māriṣa kṣurapreṇa sutīkṣṇena rājā ciccheda saṃyuge
english: Then the king, with a keenly sharpened razor-edged arrow, cut his bow with the arrow set to it, and his hand-guard too, O honored one, in the battle.

sanskrit: tad apāsya dhanuś chinnaṃ pāñcālyaḥ śatrukarśanaḥ anyad ādatta vegena dhanur bhārasahaṃ navam
english: Casting aside that severed bow, the Pāñcāla prince, harrower of foes, swiftly took up another, new and able to bear the strain.

sanskrit: prajvalann iva vegena saṃrambhād rudhirekṣaṇaḥ aśobhata maheṣvāso dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ kṛtavraṇaḥ
english: Blazing as it were with impetuosity, his eyes red with fury, the great-bowman Dhṛṣṭadyumna, though wounded, shone resplendent.

sanskrit: sa pañcadaśa nārācāñ śvasataḥ pannagān iva jighāṃsur bharataśreṣṭhaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumno vyavāsṛjat
english: He, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, seeking to slay that best of the Bharatas, let fly fifteen iron arrows like hissing serpents.

sanskrit: te varma hemavikṛtaṃ bhittvā rājñaḥ śilāśitāḥ viviśur vasudhāṃ vegāt kaṅkabarhiṇavāsasaḥ
english: Those stone-whetted shafts, fledged with heron and peacock feathers, piercing the king's gold-wrought armor, sank with force into the earth.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho mahārāja putras te 'tivyarājata vasante puṣpaśabalaḥ sapuṣpa iva kiṃśukaḥ
english: Sorely wounded, O great king, your son shone exceedingly, like a kiṃśuka tree in spring, dappled with blossoms, laden with flowers.

sanskrit: sa chinnavarmā nārācaiḥ prahārair jarjaracchaviḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnasya bhallena kruddhaś ciccheda kārmukam
english: His armor cut by the iron arrows, his form battered by the blows, he in wrath cut asunder the bow of Dhṛṣṭadyumna with a broad-headed shaft.

sanskrit: athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ tvaramāṇo mahīpatiḥ sāyakair daśabhī rājan bhruvor madhye samārdayat
english: Then, his bow cut, the lord of the earth in haste, O king, smote him with ten shafts between the brows.

sanskrit: tasya te 'śobhayan vaktraṃ karmāraparimārjitāḥ praphullaṃ campakaṃ yadvad bhramarā madhulipsavaḥ
english: Those shafts, burnished by the smith, adorned his face as bees greedy for nectar adorn a campaka in full bloom.

sanskrit: tad apāsya dhanuś chinnaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumno mahāmanāḥ anyad ādatta vegena dhanur bhallāṃś ca ṣoḍaśa
english: Casting aside that severed bow, the high-minded Dhṛṣṭadyumna swiftly took up another bow and sixteen broad-headed arrows.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanasyāśvān hatvā sūtaṃ ca pañcabhiḥ dhanuś ciccheda bhallena jātarūpapariṣkṛtam
english: Then, slaying Duryodhana's horses and his charioteer with five, he cut with a broad-headed shaft the gold-wrought bow.

sanskrit: rathaṃ sopaskaraṃ chatraṃ śaktiṃ khaḍgaṃ gadāṃ dhvajam bhallaiś ciccheda navabhiḥ putrasya tava pārṣataḥ
english: The chariot with its gear, the parasol, the spear, the sword, the mace, and the standard—the son of Pṛṣata cut all of your son's with nine broad-headed arrows.

sanskrit: tapanīyāṅgadaṃ citraṃ nāgaṃ maṇimayaṃ śubham dhvajaṃ kurupateś chinnaṃ dadṛśuḥ sarvapārthivāḥ
english: The bright standard of the Kuru lord, bearing the figure of an elephant wrought in gems and banded with refined gold, all the kings beheld cut down.

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ tu virathaṃ chinnasarvāyudhaṃ raṇe bhrātaraḥ paryarakṣanta sodaryā bharatarṣabha
english: Duryodhana, chariotless, all his weapons cut away in the battle, his own brothers guarded round about, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tam āropya rathe rājan daṇḍadhāro janādhipaṃ apovāha ca saṃbhrānto dhṛṣṭadyumnasya paśyataḥ
english: Setting that lord of men upon his car, O king, Daṇḍadhāra in alarm bore him away, before the very eyes of Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: karṇas tu sātyakiṃ jitvā rājagṛddhī mahābalaḥ droṇahantāram ugreṣuṃ sasārābhimukhaṃ raṇe
english: But Karṇa, the mighty one, coveting the king, having vanquished Sātyaki, advanced face to face in the battle against the fierce-arrowed slayer of Droṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ pṛṣṭhato 'bhyayāt tūrṇaṃ śaineyo vitudañ śaraiḥ vāraṇaṃ jaghanopānte viṣāṇābhyām iva dvipaḥ
english: The Śaineya swiftly came up behind him, goading him with shafts, as one elephant gores another in the flank with its tusks.

sanskrit: sa bhārata mahān āsīd yodhānāṃ sumahātmanām karṇapārṣatayor madhye tvadīyānāṃ mahāraṇaḥ
english: There was, O Bhārata, a mighty battle, between Karṇa and the son of Pṛṣata, in the midst of your high-souled warriors.

sanskrit: na pāṇḍavānāṃ nāsmākaṃ yodhaḥ kaś cit parāṅmukhaḥ pratyadṛśyata yat karṇaḥ pāñcālāṃs tvarito yayau
english: Neither of the Pāṇḍavas nor of ours was any warrior seen turning his back, for that Karṇa had advanced in haste upon the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: tasmin kṣaṇe naraśreṣṭha gajavājinarakṣayaḥ prādurāsīd ubhayato rājan madhyaṃgate 'hani
english: In that moment, O best of men, a destruction of elephants, steeds, and men arose on both sides, O king, when the day had reached its middle.

sanskrit: pāñcālās tu mahārāja tvaritā vijigīṣavaḥ sarvato 'bhyadravan karṇaṃ patatriṇa iva drumam
english: But the Pāñcālas, O great king, in haste and eager for victory, rushed upon Karṇa from every side, like birds upon a tree.

sanskrit: teṣām ādhirathiḥ kruddho yatamānān manasvinaḥ vicinvann eva bāṇāgraiḥ samāsādayad agrataḥ
english: The son of Adhiratha, enraged, singling them out with the points of his arrows as they strove, those resolute ones, met them head-on in the front:

sanskrit: vyāghraketuṃ suśarmāṇaṃ śaṅkuṃ cograṃ dhanaṃjayam śuklaṃ ca rocamānaṃ ca siṃhasenaṃ ca durjayam
english: Vyāghraketu and Suśarman, and Śaṅku, and Ugra, and Dhanaṃjaya, and Śukla and Rocamāna, and Siṃhasena, hard to conquer—
